title: Cosmos DB Partition Keys
description: Choose partition keys for Cosmos DB containers to balance throughput, storage, and query performance.

data.text: The **partition key** is the single most important design decision in Cosmos DB. It determines how items are distributed across physical partitions, how throughput is allocated, and how fast your queries run. A good partition key results in even storage and throughput distribution; a bad one causes hot partitions and throttling.

Cosmos DB uses a hashing algorithm on the partition key value to assign each item to a physical partition. All items with the same partition key value live in the same logical partition. Throughput and storage are divided evenly across physical partitions.

data.title: Good Partition Key Traits
items: **High cardinality** — many distinct values (e.g., userId, orderId, deviceId).
**Even distribution** — values are spread across all partitions without concentration.
**Query alignment** — your most common queries filter on the partition key.

rows: Composite key with a unique suffix
All new items hit same partition
Add a discriminator or synthetic key

data.title: Synthetic Partition Key for Time-Series Data
data.content: Combine date and sensor ID to distribute time-series writes evenly

data.title: Create a Container with Partition Key via Azure CLI
data.content: Define a container with a throughput and partition key
data.code:
az cosmosdb sql container create \
  --account-name cosmos-demo \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --database-name AppData \
  --name Orders \
  --partition-key-path '/customerId' \
  --throughput 400

terms.definition: A path in each item that determines its physical partition and throughput allocation.
A range of items within a container that share the same partition key value.
A fixed-size slice of storage (up to 50 GB) and throughput (up to 10,000 RUs) managed by Cosmos DB.
A single partition receiving disproportionate traffic, causing throttling.

data.title: Choose Once, Change Is Hard
data.text: You cannot change a container's partition key after creation. Plan carefully based on current and projected query patterns. If you need to change it, you must migrate to a new container.

data.title: Exercise: Evaluate Partition Keys
data.description: Analyze different partition key candidates for an IoT telemetry app.
steps: Given the following telemetry schema, evaluate three partition key candidates: deviceId, day, isActive.
Explain which is best and why.
Sketch a synthetic partition key if the best candidate has low cardinality at scale.
List two queries your app would run and confirm they filter on the partition key.
data.expectedOutcome: A justified partition key choice backed by cardinality and query-pattern analysis.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The partition key determines data distribution and query performance.
Align the partition key with your most common query filters.
Design carefully: partition keys cannot be changed after container creation.
data.takeaway: A good partition key is the foundation of a scalable, low-latency Cosmos DB application.
